rationale: A node identity could patch its own Node ownerReferences, causing garbage-collection deletion of itself; NodeRestriction admission did not forbid ownerReferences changes. Contract truncated, node PATCH not visible.
JWT signature verification skip flag/JWKS handling; token validation issue, not an operation-level access decision.
With default empty JWT secret the auth middleware was skipped, so anonymous requests could call protected /api/v1,v3,v4 endpoints (list/create users) that the contract declares as bearer-protected.

Authenticated caller with access to one project could GET another project's source by ID through own project URL, getting broker credentials; lookup ignored projectID. Contract truncated, sources path not visible.
Flaw is in blockchain VM built-in function authorization (CallerAddr vs RecipientAddr), not an HTTP operation of the service.
An administrator of one organization could update or delete applications, syncers, tokens and webhooks of other organizations via request body organization/ID; authz filter checked the wrong owner.
NetworkManager role was permitted backup and restore; it could POST /api/v1/restore with a tampered database and escalate to Admin, an operation reserved for higher roles.
A team admin could batch-delete certificate templates of other teams: authorization used the supplied team id but template IDs were not checked to belong to that team.
GET /api/allusers was registered on the public router group, so anonymous callers received the user list although the contract declares ApiKeyAuth and states authentication is required.
A bearer token with only pull/push scopes could DELETE manifests and blobs because DELETE was mapped to push and the fine-grained authz was bypassed for bearer auth.
Missing proposal timestamp window check (replay) in peer endorser gRPC filter; not an access-control decision over an HTTP operation.

A non-admin could call POST /api/users with the admin-role flag set and create an admin account; handler did not restrict that property to admins. Contract only states admin needed when self-registration is off.

rationale: A user with read access to one repository could obtain blobs of a repository denied by access control via dedupe cache (HEAD blob / mount) when knowing the digest.
Container network isolation default allowing MCP containers to reach host services; network/containment issue, not an access decision of an HTTP operation.
Any client with an arbitrary bearer token could GET WorkflowTemplates/ClusterWorkflowTemplates, read via server privileges; handlers lacked the per-user permission (CanI) check.
Disabled SAML identity provider still accepted in IdP-initiated broker login; login-flow/IdP configuration logic, not operation-level access control.
